classification.difficultyReason: Recognise similar shadow triangles, convert metres to centimetres and use corresponding lengths.

content.prompt: A vertical stick of length $30\text{ cm}$ casts a shadow of length $5\text{ cm}$ at 12 p.m. Find the length, in centimetres, of the shadow cast by a 1 metre ruler placed in the same position at the same time of the day.

answer.worked:
The stick and ruler form right-angled triangles with their shadows. The Sun has the same angle of elevation, so the triangles are similar (AAA).

The ruler is $100\text{ cm}$ long. Let its shadow length be $x\text{ cm}$. Matching sides give:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{x}{5}&=\frac{100}{30}\\x&=5\times\frac{100}{30}\\x&=\frac{50}{3}\\x&=16\frac{2}{3}.\end{align*}$$
The ruler casts a shadow of $16\frac{2}{3}\text{ cm}$.
